**Reasoning in character**

Me and the wife, we're 67 and 64 now. The kids haven't farmed in years — they're all in the city. So it's just the two of us, and my back isn't what it used to be. I have to think about what we can actually manage.

I've been doing wheat and maize on 10 mu my whole life. Same fields, same time every year. I'll plant wheat around October 10th — everyone in our village does, and there's no reason to change. Before planting I'll flood the field once and put down about 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu. In spring, when the wheat starts looking yellow at jointing, I'll put down half a bag of urea per mu and pump water once. Last year I skipped the third irrigation and the heads were small — I won't do that again.

After the wheat machine comes in mid-June, I need to get maize in fast. I can't do it alone anymore so I'll hire a neighbor's son to help seed the 10 mu. I'll mix some compound fertilizer in the seed furrow. When the maize is knee-high, I'll spread urea on a cloudy day. If it doesn't rain I'll pump once. The well costs money every time so I try to time it with rain when I can.

The stevia on 6.1 mu is what keeps us steady. The company sends a truck to collect, so I know I'll get paid. But harvesting 4 or 5 times a summer is brutal. Last year my wife and I hired two workers from the next village for the July harvest — cost us about 400 yuan a day. I'll have to do that again. I fertilize the stevia after each cut with a bit of urea, otherwise the next flush doesn't come back strong. Old Li next door does the same.

My biggest worry is spending too much cash early in the season. I try to keep a few hundred yuan in reserve — last year the pump motor needed repair in August and I had nothing left.
